correctness.rationale: For each spoke, its closed edge neighbourhood has size \(k\) if its arm has length one, and \(k+1\) otherwise; the corresponding red-count constraint is exactly \(R\in\{1,k-1\}\) or \(R+b_i\in\{1,k\}\). For \(k\ge3\) these force precisely \(R\in\{0,1,k-1,k\}\), with fixed second-edge colours. On each path, every interior triple must be nonmonochromatic and the last pair must differ, yielding the independent Fibonacci completion counts \(F_{L-2}\) and \(F_{L-1}\), including the \(L=2\) boundary. Disjoint central cases give the complete \(N_2(S)\) count. Positivity gives the precise obstruction, and an explicit depth-modulo-three edge colouring bounds the index by three. The standalone independent edge-neighbourhood enumerator reproduced the formula on 356 profiles (300 systematic, 56 sampled); these finite checks do not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: The accepted statement is a complete labelled two-colour edge-colouring enumerator and its sharp arm-length threshold for all spiders of arbitrary arm lengths. Kamyczura–Meszka–Przybyło (arXiv:2203.02040) provides tree upper bounds, Guo–Li–Li–Li (arXiv:2409.10899) gives a characterization for trees without degree-two vertices and only a sufficient condition with degree-two vertices, and Jin–Gao (arXiv:2604.24183) gives the bipartite upper bound and a general binary-edge-subset feasibility reformulation. None of their inspected specific theorem statements or proofs gives the Fibonacci enumeration or the exact mixed-length spider obstruction. Logical application of the general feasibility reformulation still requires solving and counting nontrivial compatible local arm states. Search nonappearance is not a proof of uniqueness; unindexed equivalent formulae remain a risk.

value.rationale: The long-standing two-versus-three question for conflict-free edge colouring of trees is resolved exactly on a natural all-subdivisions class. The sharp obstruction depends only on the coexistence of pendant arms and multiple once-subdivided arms, a structural statement not predicted by the general upper bounds. The closed Fibonacci formula counts every labelled optimum two-colouring for arbitrary arm lengths and exposes how local path constraints couple through the high-degree vertex. This is a complete natural classification and enumerator, not an arbitrary finite parameter slice, a routine restatement of feasibility, or an experimental guess.
